title: Multi-head windowed rerank parallelism to cut tail latency
creator: Asha Patel
description: Problem: The reranker endpoint is showing high tail latency (p99 spikes > 1.8s) for multi-candidate scoring workloads, especially when candidate token lengths vary. Current implementation decodes candidates serially inside a single microbatch which causes long-running requests to block smaller candidates and prevents efficient batching. Scope: Implement a multi-head execution model that splits candidate sets into parallel scoring heads, uses a windowed per-head token budget, and applies a soft timebox per request to avoid blocking the serving thread pool. Goals: reduce p99 by >=30% for typical workloads, keep p50 stable, maintain or improve overall GPU utilization, and avoid increased error rates or quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: 1) End-to-end rerank p99 latency reduced by >=30% on benchmark dataset V2; 2) No increase in classification errors or ranking regressions beyond 0.5% compared to baseline; 3) Resource overhead <= 15% extra GPU cycles on production mix; 4) Canary rollout with automatic fallback to single-head if timeboxes triggered >2% of requests.
design_notes:
- Split candidates into N parallel heads (configurable; default 3) per request. Each head runs an independent decode loop with its own KV cache slice.
- Windowed token budget: allocate token budget in small windows (e.g., 8 tokens) and round-robin across heads to reduce long-tail single-candidate blockers.
- Per-request soft timebox: stop decoding low-probability candidates after the timebox and mark them for conservative scoring (e.g., truncated logits + fallback rerank heuristic).
- Scheduler: capacity-aware queue that considers token-length distribution and per-customer priority. Use existing batching infrastructure and add backpressure tokens to avoid OOM on heavy requests.
- KV prefetching: warm KV caches for candidate heads using prefix hashes to avoid first-token stalls.
Tradeoffs: additional inter-head coordination increases CPU overhead and complexity in KV sharding; aggressive timeboxing risks small accuracy regressions which we'll monitor with evaluation sets.
implementation_plan:
Phase 1 (Spike & prototype): build a prototype in the rerank worker that can run 2 heads concurrently and measure p50/p95/p99 on lab traffic. (Owner: Miguel)
Phase 2 (Controlled experiments): add windowed token budget, integrate per-request timebox, run A/B tests on 10% of staging traffic. Add metrics for timebox hits and per-head utilization. (Owner: Miguel, Timeline: 2 weeks)
Phase 3 (Canary rollout): deploy to Canary cluster with fallback flag to single-head. Observe for 48h and check dashboards. Roll forward to 25% then 100% if stable. (Owner: SRE + Miguel)
Phase 4 (Post-rollout): tune defaults (heads, window, timebox), add automatic fallback policies in routing layer.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: Increased GPU fragmentation and small kernel inefficiencies. Mitigation: measure utilization and, if needed, coalesce small heads into multi-request microbatches.
- Risk: Timeboxes causing ranking regressions. Mitigation: conservative default timebox and regression monitoring tied to eval prompt sets; immediate rollback flag in console.
- Risk: KV cache thrash due to sharded slices. Mitigation: implement LRU-prefetch and watermarks in the KV layer and monitor miss rates.
